description:
Front elevation: The Type M controller cabinet is drawn as a rectangular enclosure 30" wide, with a roof overhang at the top and a small lifting-plate lug at each upper corner (arrow callout 'Removable lifting plate per S-68.1 if required'). The cabinet stands a minimum (MIN.) of 48" high above the foundation. The door has a hinge on the right edge and a handle on the left. A boxed callout in the upper door reads 'Cutout for Police door if required'. Three groups of three horizontal louver slots at the bottom of the door are called out 'Filtered ventilating louvers'. The door opening is dimensioned 26" wide.

Side elevation: The side of the cabinet is 48" MIN. high with a sloped roof that rises toward the back and has an overhanging front lip. A removable lifting plate per S-68.1 sits on the roof, shown 2" high with a 1/2" D dimension below it. The depth of the cabinet is dimensioned D = 16" MIN.

Anchor bolt layout (plan): A rectangle with two anchor bolt slots on a horizontal centerline. The slots are 12 3/8" apart and the centerline is 15" from the bottom edge of the rectangle.

Table: Type M cabinet uses Foundation F-12A.

Title block: Cabinet, Controller, Type M. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Donald R. Howery, General Manager, approved August 2, 1982 (stamped 9/87). Drawing No. S-75.5.3. Revisions: add removable lifting plate (1-22-83), added notes (6-5-90, revision 1), update specification number (2-16-05, revision 2). Printed page number 71.
notes:
Revision 1 note:
1. When this cabinet is used as an ATSAC type I communication cabinet, a one-inch (1") screened drain pipe shall be provided through the foundation. A 19" x 33" or larger 3/4-inch thick plywood mounting panel shall be installed on the inside of the rear wall. Machine screws and bolts shall not protrude beyond the outside wall of the cabinet.

Callouts: Cutout for police door if required. Filtered ventilating louvers. Removable lifting plate per S-68.1 if required. Anchor bolt layout. Door opening 26". D = 16" minimum (MIN.).

Revision 2: Specification No. 92-044-04 or latest revision.

Foundation table: Type M, Foundation F-12A.
title: Type M Controller Cabinet
summary: Shows the Type M controller cabinet (Drawing S-75.5.3) with a front elevation, side elevation and anchor bolt layout. The cabinet is 30 in. wide, at least 48 in. high and at least 16 in. deep, with filtered louvers, an optional police door cutout and an optional removable lifting plate per S-68.1. It sits on a Type F-12A foundation. When used as an ATSAC type I communication cabinet, a 1 in. screened drain pipe and a 19 in. x 33 in. plywood panel are required. See Specification No. 92-044-04 or latest revision.

description:
Front view: Elevation of the Type II communication cabinet on its concrete foundation. The cabinet is 12" wide and 43-7/8" tall overall, with a cabinet opening 10" wide and 35-1/2" tall and a door panel 38" tall. A continuous stainless steel hinge runs down the left edge. A 'CITY OF LOS ANGELES' label is on the door. Two 3" PVC conduits (2-3" PVC CONDUITS) enter the foundation below the cabinet. The foundation stands 2" above the ground surface and extends 24" below that, with a break line indicating the full depth is not drawn. Anchor bolts with nuts are shown at each side of the cabinet base.

Rear view: Elevation 12" wide showing venting louvers with protective screens, in two banks of three rows by two columns, one near the top and one near the bottom of the cabinet. A removable staple for a padlock is on the right edge. A 1" drain pipe and a 1/2" DIA. x 8' ground rod come up through the foundation. The foundation is 2" above grade and 24" deep as in the front view.

Side view: Cabinet depth is 7-1/4". A 1-1/2" x 1-1/2" x 1/4" thick aluminum mounting flange is welded to the cabinet base. A 3/4" plywood panel inside the cabinet is 33" tall. Adjustable panel mounting studs are shown at the top and bottom of the panel, with 4-15/16" from the top of the cabinet to the upper stud, 6-1/16" from the bottom to the lower stud and 1-5/8" stud offset. A removable staple for padlock is at the door side. Conduits and the ground rod are shown dashed through the foundation, with a 14" MIN. dimension.

Plan view: Dimensions shown are 20" and 12" across the top, 14" across the bottom, 12" and 7-1/4" along the left side, and 8-1/8" and 4" along the right side. The drawing shows the foundation outline, the cabinet outline with mounting flange and slotted bolt holes at each side, the plywood panel with adjustable studs, and dashed circular openings for the conduits, drain pipe and ground rod.

Isometric view: A perspective of the cabinet with its door open, standing on the mounting flange base with slotted bolt holes.

Title block: Type II Communication Cabinet and Foundation. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, S. E. Rowe, General Manager, approved 2-22-91. Drawing No. S-75.0C. Drawn RMO 12-20-90, checked ERA 1-10-91, supervised JEM 1-14-91. Revisions: Supercedes S-75.0B (ERA 2-12-91), and revision ERA: Show fnd. 2" above surface (JEM 2-27-91). Printed page number 72.
notes:
NOTES:
Material: .125" thick AL 5052 H32.
Finish: anodized per MIL-A-8625C specification.
Spec. No. 92-067-02.

Callouts: Continuous hinge, stainless steel. Venting louvers with protective screens. Removable staple for padlock. Adjustable panel mounting studs. 2-3" PVC conduits. 3/4" plywood panel. 1" drain pipe. 1/2" DIA. x 8' ground rod. 1-1/2" x 1-1/2" x 1/4" thick aluminum mounting flange welded to cabinet.

Revision note: Supercedes S-75.0B. Show foundation 2" above surface.
title: Type II Communication Cabinet and Foundation
summary: Drawing S-75.0C showing the front, rear, side and plan views and an isometric of the Type II communication cabinet and its foundation. The cabinet is 12 in. wide, 7-1/4 in. deep and 43-7/8 in. tall, set on a foundation 2 in. above grade and 24 in. deep. It has a continuous stainless steel hinge, screened louvers, a padlock staple, a 3/4 in. plywood panel with adjustable studs, two 3 in. PVC conduits, a 1 in. drain pipe and an 8 ft ground rod. Material is .125 in. AL 5052 H32 with anodized finish per MIL-A-8625C, Spec. No. 92-067-02.

description:
Plan view of lid: A rounded-rectangle pull box lid with an inner recessed panel. Text 'TRAFFIC SIGNAL' is cast or stamped across the lid with a small rectangle symbol at each end of the text. A callout reads '1" letters cast or stamped in lid'.

Section: A cross section at the box edge, below a 'Finish grade' line. A concrete box wall is shown at each side, 12" tall with a stepped inner face. A concrete lid spans the top with a semicircular notch near each end. Dimensions: 2" MIN. lid bearing at each wall, 5" MIN. from the lid underside down to the conduit, 2" MIN. below that, 6" MIN. from the wall to the edge of the base, 12" wall height and 24" MIN. overall depth to the bottom of the rock bed. A conduit enters at each side, bending down and away, with a bell end inside the box, marked 'See Note 3'. The box sits on a bed of 1" crushed rock.

Title block: Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-78.5.1. Drawn MT 11-8-11, Pr. T. E. SS 12-8-11. Approved 12-8-11, signed for Jaime de la Vega, General Manager. Printed page number 73.
notes:
NOTES:
1. Pullbox details not shown on this plan shall conform to Department (Dept.) of Public Works Standard Drawing # L-201-0.
2. Outside dimension: Type PB2 is 15" x 25", Type PB3 is 22" x 34".
3. Galvanized conduits must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.

Callouts: 1" letters cast or stamped in lid. Finish grade. 1" crushed rock.
title: Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3
summary: Drawing S-78.5.1 showing the lid and a cross section of the LADOT Type PB-2 and PB-3 pull boxes. The lid is cast or stamped with 1 in. letters reading TRAFFIC SIGNAL. The section shows the concrete walls and lid, conduit entries and a 1 in. crushed rock base. Outside dimensions are 15 in. x 25 in. for PB-2 and 22 in. x 34 in. for PB-3, and conduits are bonded with ground strap or spliced #8 green grounds.

description:
Plan view of cover: A rounded-rectangle steel cover with the text 'TRAFFIC SIGNAL' embossed across it. A lift hole is at the left of the text and a hold-down bolt (hex head) at each of the left and right edges, the right one noted 'Hold-down bolt See Note 8'. The outer frame is 2'-11 1/2" +/- long and the cover is 2'-9" +/- long. The overall width is 2'-6" +/- 1" with a 1'-8" +/- inner width. A dashed inner outline marks the plate, dimensioned 1'-11 1/2" +/- by 1'-5" +/- 1". Callouts: Lift hole. Hold-down bolt. Pull box reinforced with galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Reinforced 1/2" MIN steel plate cover, galvanized after fabrication, See Notes 3 & 6.

Section: A cross section of the pull box set in the ground. A galvanized Z-bar welded frame carries the steel plate cover, which is flush with finished grade ('Top flush with finished grade (See Note 5)'). The cover is secured with a 1/2" length sleeve nut with brass bolt. A pull box concrete shell (PCC) surrounds the box, with a stepped lower edge. A bonding jumper (See Note 7) connects from the cover to the conduit grounding bushings, shown as a looped braided strap. Two conduits enter at an angle through the bottom with grounding bushings, and the box rests on a bed of 1" crushed rock. Dimensions: 1'-0" MIN wall depth below grade, 2" and 6" MIN at the footing step, 6" MIN all around and 3" MIN all around for the special concrete footing outside the box.

Title block: Metal Cover Traffic Pull Box [Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T)], sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-78.5.2. Drawn MT 05-10-07, T.E. JV 2-11-08, Sr. T.E. JW 2-13-08, Pr. T.E. SS 2-13-08. Approved June 26, 2008, signed for Rita L. Robinson, General Manager. Printed page number 74.
notes:
NOTES:
1. Traffic pullboxes in driveways, alleys and locations with vehicular traffic shall be metal covered per this standard.
2. Pullbox details not shown on this plan shall conform to Caltrans Standard Plan ES-8.
3. Traffic pullbox shall be provided with steel cover and special concrete footing. Steel cover shall have embossed non-skid pattern.
4. Galvanized conduits must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.
5. Top of pull boxes shall be flush with surrounding grade or top of adjacent curb, except that in unpaved areas where pull box is not immediately adjacent to and protected by a concrete foundation, pole or other protective construction, the box shall be placed with its top 1 1/4" above surrounding grade. Where practicable, pull boxes shown in the vicinity of curbs shall be placed adjacent to the back of curb, and pull boxes shown adjacent to standards shall be placed on side of foundation facing away from traffic, unless otherwise noted. When pull box is installed in sidewalk area, the depth of the pull box shall be adjusted so that the top of the pull box is flush with the sidewalk.
6. Pull box cover shall be marked as "TRAFFIC SIGNAL".
7. Bonding jumper for metal covers shall be flat braided strap, 2' long minimum, Panduit Part # BS202446EU or equivalent.
8. Hold-down bolt shall be 5/8" and coarse threaded.

Callouts: Lift hole. Hold-down bolt. Pull box reinforced with galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Reinforced 1/2" minimum (MIN) steel plate cover, galvanized after fabrication, see Notes 3 and 6. Galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Pull box. Bonding jumper, see Note 7. PCC (portland cement concrete). Grounding bushing. 1/2" length sleeve nut with brass bolt. Top flush with finished grade (see Note 5). 6" MIN all around. 3" MIN all around. 1" crushed rock.
title: Metal Cover Traffic Pull Box (Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T))
summary: Drawing S-78.5.2 showing the plan and section of the LADOT metal cover traffic pull box, equivalent to Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T). It has a reinforced 1/2 in. minimum galvanized steel cover marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL on a Z-bar frame, a concrete footing, a bonding jumper to the conduit grounding bushings and a 1 in. crushed rock base. Metal covered boxes are required in driveways, alleys and where vehicles travel. Remaining details follow Caltrans Standard Plan ES-8.

description:
Plan view: A rectangular special cover seen from above inside its frame, with a wavy break line showing the cover cut away at the right. 'SIGNAL' is lettered at the center and a centerline passes through two lifting holes marked '2-3/4" Brass lift plug'. Callout 2 (revision triangle) points to '1" Stamped letters'. Variable dimensions are lettered: "A" is the cover outside width, "B" the frame inside width, "C" the frame inside length, "D" the distance from the top edge of the frame to the centerline. A 4" typical band marks the steel plate frame width.

Cover elevation: The cover is dimensioned "E" overall at the top with 3" typical from the end to each lift plug, and "F" at the bottom, with a beveled (sloped) edge. Cover thickness is 1 13/16".

Section through frame and cover (8 degree detail): The frame and cover edges are sloped at 8 degrees from vertical on all four sides. A 3/16" plate forms the cover and a 4" x 3/16" steel plate forms the frame, with 1/8" typical clearance between them. The cover rests on a 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar, welded with a 3/16" fillet weld, 3" long, at the end and mid-point (typical). The height shown is 1 13/16".

Lift plug detail: A steel sleeve with internal thread 3/4"-10 UNC, full length, to match the brass lift plug. The plug has a 3/8" square slot, 3/8" deep. The cover plate is 3/16" steel plate and the plug depth is 5/8" with 3/16" below, within a total thickness of 1 13/16". A 3/16" weld symbol is shown at the sleeve.

Section in sidewalk: The frame sits flush with sidewalk grade over the pull box. Dimensions: "C" frame inside across the top, "G" frame inside across the base, 1 13/16", 2 3/16" and 4" depths, a 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar, and 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical on all sides. Concrete surrounds the frame above the pull box.

Table of dimensions:
For Type 2 Pullbox: A = 18 3/4", B = 19", C = 29", D = 9 1/2", E = 28 3/4", F = 28 1/4", G = 27 7/8".
For Type 3 Pullbox: A = 25 3/4", B = 26", C = 38", D = 13", E = 37 3/4", F = 37 1/4", G = 36 7/8". Revision 1 applies to the table.

Slot 3/8" square and 3/8" deep. 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical all sides. Typical all four (4) sides of frame and cover. End and mid-point (typical). Sidewalk grade. Pull box.
title: Special Cover for Pull Box
summary: Drawing S-78.8 showing the galvanized steel special frame and cover for Type 2 and Type 3 pull boxes in sidewalk. Plan, elevation, an 8 degree sloped-edge section and a lift plug detail are given, with a table of dimensions A to G for each pull box type. description:
Plan view of lid: The precast splice box shown from above with a sloped outer frame (PCC or other material approved by the engineer) around a diamond-plate steel parkway cover. The cover is marked 'LADOT' and has two 3/4" lifting holes and notches at its edges. Callouts: 3/4" lifting holes. 3/16" diamond plate steel parkway cover 2'-0" x 3'-0". 1" dia. pick holes.

Section: The box top is flush with pavement. Above it is a 6" top, including frame height, with RPM cover 2'-0" x 3'-0", set in PCC or other material approved by the engineer. Below it is the riser and the base section. The interior width is 44" and the walls are 6" thick. Conduit enters through the walls at holes sealed with approved compound after installing the conduit, and is shown as 'CONDUIT TO TERMINATION PULLBOX'. The base sits on a 12" MIN. layer of 1" clean crushed rock sump.

Isometric of cover: A 3/16" diamond plate steel parkway cover 2'-0" x 3'-0" is shown with an L-shaped cutout, an angle frame underneath and 1" dia. pick holes.

Isometric of frame: A 2'-0" x 3'-0" opening frame, 6" tall, called '6" top incl. frame height w/ RPM cover 2'-0" x 3'-0"', sloped outward to the base.

Isometric of riser: Overall 2'-8" x 3'-8", 6" tall, with a 2'-0" x 3'-0" opening, an 8" notch dimension and a 4" wall. Callout: Riser.

Isometric of base section: Overall 18" tall, with 4 lifting inserts (2 each side) and two lifting holes, shown cut away. Walls are precast reinforced concrete. 4" x 8" knockouts, 2 pcs each side wall. 8" x 11" knockouts, 2 pcs each end wall.

title: Fiber Optic Splice Box I
summary: Drawing S-79.02A showing the precast reinforced concrete Fiber Optic Splice Box I with a plan of its 3/16 in. diamond plate steel parkway cover, a section and isometrics of the cover, frame, riser and base. description:
Plan view of lid: The precast splice box shown from above with a sloped frame (PCC or other material approved by the engineer) around a diamond-plate steel parkway cover marked 'LADOT', with two 3/4" lifting holes and edge notches. Callout: 3/4" lifting holes.

The overall width of the top is 44" and the walls are 6" thick, with a stepped inner face and a notched base that holds a small recess at the center of the sloped floor. It has 4 lifting inserts (2 each side), a 6" dia. sump in the floor, two 1" dia. ground rod knockouts, and 2 pull irons 7/8" dia. 8" x 16" knockouts (2 each side) are shown as a grid of rectangles on the side wall.

title: Fiber Optic Splice Box II
summary: Drawing S-79.02B showing the larger precast Fiber Optic Splice Box II, with a plan of its diamond plate steel parkway cover, a section and isometrics of the cover, frame, riser and base. The base is 2'-11" tall, 2'-8" x 3'-8" overall, with a 6 in. dia. sump, two 7/8 in. pull irons, two 1 in. ground rod knockouts and 8 in. x 16 in. knockouts on each side. It sits on a 12 in. minimum bed of 1 in. crushed rock.

description:
Top view: A rectangular 4 in. thick slab 24" wide by 96" long, with the long dimension divided 36", 24", 36" along the curb face (shown as a double line along the left edge). A 4-bolt pattern lies at the center of the middle 24" square on an 8 1/2" bolt circle, with diagonals at 45 degrees to the centerline. A dashed conduit stub runs from the center to the right side of the slab. Callouts: 4" thick slab (two places), 8 1/2" bolt circle, Curb Face.

Elevation: A pole stands on a 10" x 10" x 3/4" base plate with 1" diameter anchor bolts, set on mortar over a concrete footing. The pole carries a 3" x 5" reinforced hand hole and cover, with the hand hole rim 1" +/- 1/4" above the base plate level and 8" above finished grade. A 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding is welded inside the pole shaft at 180 degrees from the hand hole rim, and a #8 green bonding wire runs from it down to the anchor bolt. The mortar bed between base plate and footing is 2" minimum (MIN.) to 3" maximum (MAX.) thick and is finished with a slope from 45 degrees to 90 degrees including drain holes. A curb face is shown at the left. The footing is 24" x 24" (24" diameter optional) and 42" deep, with a 4" minimum topping (minimum 14" MIN. dimension from grade to the conduit elbow) and a 3" MIN. dimension at the bottom of the footing. Anchor bolts are 1" diameter x 3'-0" long with the bottom 6" threaded, and an anchor plate 10" x 10" x 3/4" at the bottom, with 2 nuts and 2 washers each. A conduit rises in the center and bends to exit the side (See notes 1 and 2).

Title block: Foundation Type F-1 & F-8, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.1. Drawn MT 9-30-15, T.E. JV 9-30-15, Sr. T.E. MA 10-1-15, Pr. T.E. VJ 10-2-15. Approved 11-20-15, Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager. Bureau of Engineering, Structural Engineering Division block: City Engineer Gary Lee Moore, PE, Env SP; structural design checked by Peter Chiu, SE; approved by Shailesh Patel, SE, Division Engineer, 1-26-16. Printed page number 79.
notes:
Notes:
1. Type F-1: 2" nominal size conduit, unless otherwise specified.
2. Type F-8 and Type F-8A: 3" nominal size conduit, unless otherwise specified.
3. Unless otherwise specified, in unpaved areas a 36" x 24" x 4" slab shall be provided for each door opening in the case of a model 336 cabinet.
4. On Type F-8 and Type F-8A, ground rod shall be installed in controller pullbox.

Callouts: 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding welded to interior of pole shaft at 180 degrees from hand hole rim. #8 green bonding wire. Anchor bolt: thread top 8" and galvanize 12" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt), total 4. Base plate 10" x 10" x 3/4". 2" minimum to 3" maximum mortar. Curb face. After plumbing standard, place mortar all around bolts. Finish with slope ranging from 45 degrees to 90 degrees including drain holes. 1" dia. x 3'-0" anchor bolts, thread bottom 6" (2 nuts and 2 washers, total 4 required per bolt). Anchor plate 10" x 10" x 3/4". Pole. 3" x 5" reinforced hand hole and cover. Finished grade. 4" minimum topping. 42". 14" minimum. 3" minimum. 24" x 24", 24" dia. optional.
title: Foundation, Types F-1 and F-8
summary: Drawing S-52.1 showing the LADOT Type F-1 and F-8 signal and lighting pole foundation, a 24 in. x 24 in. (24 in. diameter optional) concrete footing 42 in. deep with four 1 in. anchor bolts on an 8 1/2 in. bolt circle, a 10 in. x 10 in. x 3/4 in. base plate and a mortar bed. A 36 in. x 24 in. x 36 in. long 4 in. slab layout is given in top view. F-1 uses 2 in. conduit and F-8 and F-8A use 3 in. conduit, and a #8 green bonding wire grounds the pole.

description:
Top view: A 32" square footing with an 8 1/8" square anchor bolt pattern on an 11 1/2" bolt circle, with diagonals at 45 degrees. A center conduit and a bonding conduit are drawn at the middle and conduit stubs, shown dashed, extend out to the right and bottom. A 36" dimension is given from the left of the footing outline to the conduit centerline.

Section: A concrete footing 32" square in plan and 48" deep with a minimum topping 4" thick above and 14" MIN. to the top of the conduit elbow. Four anchor bolts 1 1/8" x 40" x 4" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt) are set in a square pattern with a bonding strap or wire tied to them. A center conduit with a bushing rises 2 3/4" above the topping and another conduit curves out the side. A curb is shown at the left. A 6" MIN. dimension is given at the bottom right of the footing.

Title block: Foundation, Type F-2, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.2. Drawn MT 03-30-04, T.E. JV 6-1-06, Sr. T.E. JW 6-1-06, Pr. T.E. SS 6-2-06. Approved June 2, 2006, Gloria J. Jeff, General Manager. Printed page number 80.
notes:
Notes:
1. Use 1" galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2" schedule 80 PVC conduit for traffic signal unless otherwise specified.

3. Topping shall be considered as a part of the foundation.

Callouts: 11 1/2" bolt circle. 32" square. 8 1/8" square. 36". Bonding strap or wire. Bushing. 2 3/4". Minimum topping 4". 14" minimum. 48". 6" minimum. Anchor bolts 1 1/8" x 40" x 4" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt).
title: Foundation, Type F-2
summary: Drawing S-52.2 showing the LADOT Type F-2 foundation for a signal mast arm pole, a 32 in. square concrete footing 48 in. deep with four 1 1/8 in. anchor bolts on an 8 1/8 in. square pattern and an 11 1/2 in. bolt circle. It has a 4 in. minimum topping, a bonding strap or wire and conduit stubs. Use 1 in. galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2 in. schedule 80 PVC for traffic signal.

description:
Top view: A circular drilled shaft 30" diameter with a 2" clearance ring to the reinforcing. A bold circle shows the reinforcing cage with 12 longitudinal bars (#7, total 12) and a spiral or hoop of #4 bars. An 8 1/8" square anchor bolt pattern lies on an 11 1/2" bolt circle with diagonals at 45 degrees. Conduit stubs, shown dashed, run to the right and bottom. A 36" dimension runs from the left side of the section to the centerline.

Section: A cast-in-drilled-hole (CIDH) concrete shaft of 560-C-3250 concrete with a curb and sidewalk at the left. A reinforcing cage 26" diameter (O.D.) and overall height 4'-6" or 6'-9" has #7 vertical bars and #4 spiral ties. Four anchor bolts 1 1/8" x 40" x 4" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt) are set inside the cage with a bonding strap or wire. A conduit with bushing rises 2 3/4" clear above the topping. Dimensions: 4" topping, 3" clear above the cage, 18" MIN. to the top of the conduit stub, and 3" clear at the bottom. Shaft depth is 5' with 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to the foundation, or 7'-3" without 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to the foundation.

Title block: CIDH Foundation, Type F-2, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.2.2. Drawn MT 11-8-04, T.E. JV 6-1-06, Sr. T.E. JW 6-1-06, Pr. T.E. SS 6-2-06. Approved June 2, 2006, Gloria J. Jeff, General Manager. Printed page number 81.
notes:
Notes:
1. Use 1" galvanized conduit for street lighting and 2" schedule 80 PVC conduit for traffic signal unless otherwise specified.
2. Conduit stubs from foundation shall be in the direction of the nearest corresponding pullbox unless otherwise specified.

Callouts: 30" dia. 8 1/8" square. 2" clearance. #7 total 12. #4 at 6" or #4 spiral at 6" pitch with 1'-6" lap at splice. 11 1/2" bolt circle. Bonding strap or wire. Bushing. 560-C-3250 concrete. Anchor bolts 1 1/8" x 40" x 4" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt). Reinforcing cage 26" dia. (O.D.), overall height 4'-6" or 6'-9". 5' with 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to foundation. 7'-3" without 100 sq-ft (minimum) concrete sidewalk adjacent to foundation. 3" clear. 2 3/4" clear.
title: CIDH Foundation, Type F-2
summary: Drawing S-52.2.2 showing the cast-in-drilled-hole Type F-2 foundation, a 30 in. diameter shaft of 560-C-3250 concrete with a 26 in. diameter reinforcing cage of twelve #7 bars and #4 spiral at 6 in. pitch. Shaft depth is 5 ft with at least 100 sq-ft of adjacent concrete sidewalk, or 7 ft 3 in. without it. Four 1 1/8 in. x 40 in. anchor bolts sit on an 11 1/2 in. bolt circle with a bonding strap and conduit stubs.

description:
Top view: An 18" square footing with a 4 1/2" bolt circle holding four anchor bolts on diagonals at 45 degrees. A dashed conduit stub runs from the center to the right. A 36" dimension runs from the left side of the curb to the centerline.

Section: An 18" wide concrete footing with a minimum 3" topping, a bushing on the center conduit extending 1 3/8" above the topping, a bonding strap or wire, and a curb and sidewalk at the left. Four anchor bolts 1/2" x 10 1/2" x 1 1/2" (2 nuts and 2 washers per bolt required) are cast in. Dimensions: 14" MIN. from the top of the footing to the conduit stub and 18" overall depth.

Title block: Foundation, Type F-7, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.7. Drawn MT 03-05-04, Pr. T.E. TLJ 02-09-05. Approved February 25, 2005, Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager. Printed page number 82.

title: Foundation, Type F-7
summary: Drawing S-52.7 showing the small LADOT Type F-7 foundation, an 18 in. square concrete footing 18 in. deep with a 3 in. minimum topping. It has four 1/2 in. x 10 1/2 in. x 1 1/2 in. anchor bolts on a 4 1/2 in. bolt circle, a bushing, a bonding strap or wire and a 1 in. nominal conduit.

description:
Exploded isometric: Shows how a pedestrian push button (PPB) post is mounted on an existing F-1 to F-7 foundation using the adapter plate. From top to bottom: the PPB post with its own square base plate bolted by four studs with nuts and washers, the adapter plate with four slotted corner ears fastened to the foundation anchor bolts (two washers each anchor bolt, with a nut), the conduit stub rising from the foundation, and the foundation block below. Callouts: PPB Post. Two washers each anchor bolt. Adapter plate. Conduit. Foundation (spelled 'Fountation' on the sheet).

Side view of plate: The adapter plate is a flat 3/8" steel plate with two 5/8" x 1 3/4" square or hex head galvanized bolts projecting up from it, with nuts below. A 1/4" fillet weld is shown at each of the two bolts, noted 'Fillet weld at least two opposite flats of each bolt'.

Plan view of plate: The plate is a 10 1/2" x 10 1/2" square with four slotted corner ears on a 9 1/2" diameter bolt circle, a 4 1/2" diameter circle through the four post bolt holes and a 3" diameter center opening. A 1 3/8" slot width is shown at the upper right ear.

Title block: Adapter Base Plate (For F-1 to F-7 Foundation). City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Donald R. Howery, General Manager. Approved May 27, 1971, B. Fredrickson for General Manager. Drawing No. S-52.7.1. Spec. No. 92-056-01. Printed page number 83.
notes:
Note:
Base plate shall be hot dipped galvanized after machining in accordance with the latest edition of ASTM designation A-123.

Spec. No. 92-056-01.

Callouts: PPB (pedestrian push button) post. Two washers each anchor bolt. Adapter plate. Conduit. Foundation. 5/8" x 1 3/4" square or hex head galvanized bolts. 3/8" steel plate. 1/4" fillet weld at least two opposite flats of each bolt. 10 1/2" x 10 1/2". 4 1/2" dia. 9 1/2" dia. 3" dia. 1 3/8".
title: Adapter Base Plate (For F-1 to F-7 Foundation)
summary: Drawing S-52.7.1 showing the 10 1/2 in. square, 3/8 in. thick steel adapter base plate used to mount a pedestrian push button (PPB) post on an F-1 to F-7 foundation. An exploded isometric shows the post, plate, washers, nuts, conduit and foundation, and a plan shows the slotted corners on a 9 1/2 in. circle. The plate is hot dipped galvanized after machining per ASTM A-123.

description:
Plan view: A rectangular foundation top 22" wide and about 39" long, with a 36" slab (per Note 2) beyond one end shown dashed with a break line and a 36" dimension from the centerline to the curb face along the bottom. Inside the 22" outline an 18" inner rectangle shows the chamfered top. Two anchor bolts are 12" apart (6" each side of centerline) and three circles on the centerline show the two 3" conduits and the ground rod. Other dimensions: 6" MIN. from the end of the foundation to the nearest circle and 8" MIN. from the centerline to the foundation edge. Callouts: Slab per note 2. Curb face.

Section: A tapered concrete foundation 35" wide at the top and 39" wide at the base, 8" above sidewalk grade and 24" below it, with the top 3" above the plate and bushings. Two bushings and a bonding strap or wire are shown on the top plate. Two 3" conduits rise from the foundation and bend out the side 14" MIN. below sidewalk grade, with a 6" MIN. dimension at the base. Two anchor bolts 5/8" dia. x 16"L (including 2" bend) project 2" above the top. A 1/2" dia. x 8'-0" copper weld ground rod extends below the foundation.

Title block: Foundation, Type F-12A, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.1.2B. Drawn MT 5-07-08, Pr. T.E. SS 6-26-08. Approved June 26, 2008, Rita L. Robinson, General Manager. Printed page number 84.
notes:
NOTES:
1. Conduit consists of (2) 3" nominal size unless otherwise specified.
2. Slab shall be constructed as per Standard Specification for Public Works Construction, section 302-6, latest edition.

title: Foundation, Type F-12A
summary: Drawing S-52.1.2B showing the LADOT Type F-12A foundation used for the Type M controller cabinet. It is a tapered concrete block 8 in. above and 24 in. below sidewalk grade, 35 in. wide at top and 39 in. at base, with two 3 in. conduits, two 5/8 in. anchor bolts, two bushings, a bonding strap and an 8 ft copper weld ground rod. A slab per Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction section 302-6 is placed beside it.

description:
Top view: A 30" long by 24" wide foundation seen from above, set 36" back from a curb (curb shown as two parallel lines with break marks at each end). A 36" slab in unpaved area, also 24" wide, is shown at each end of the foundation. Four anchor bolt locations are laid out 25" apart along the length and 15" apart across the width, 4 1/2" typical from the long edges and 2 1/2" typical from the end, with 9" from the rear bolts to the rear edge. Two conduit risers and a ground rod hole are shown, with two conduits running dashed to the rear through the rear slab and labeled 'TO #3 PULLBOX'. The rear slab is labeled 'MOUNT REARSIDE OF CABINET'.

Side view: The foundation is 30" long and 18" tall, projecting 5 1/2" above the adjacent unpaved slab and 2" above the bushing plane. 4 anchor bolts 3/4" x 15" x 2" (4 required) project from the top. A 1/2" dia x 8'-0" copper weld ground rod runs down through the foundation. A bushing sits on the conduit riser. Two 3" conduits (2-3" CONDUIT) bend out of the foundation toward the pullbox at a depth of 14" MIN. below the adjacent slab surface.

Title block: Foundation, Type F-332, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-52.1.3. Drawn MT 11-8-11, Pr. T.E. SS 12-8-11. Approved 12-8-11, signed for Jaime de la Vega, General Manager. Printed page number 85.

title: Foundation, Type F-332
summary: Drawing S-52.1.3 showing the LADOT Type F-332 foundation for a 332 controller cabinet, a 30 in. x 24 in. concrete block 18 in. deep with four 3/4 in. anchor bolts, an 8 ft copper weld ground rod and two 3 in. conduits to a #3 pullbox. 36 in. x 24 in. slabs are placed at the front and rear in unpaved areas and no pullbox may be located within them. Grounding details are on S-79.9B.

description:
Wiring diagram: Across the top is a Pullbox Cover labeled 'Service T.S. & S.L.' (traffic signal and street lighting). Below it, three 'Alum. wires by DWP' (3 #2) drop from the service pole, the center one marked Neutral. At the end of each, 6 #6 standard copper wires (12" long) by DWP are spliced. Each of the two outer legs splits into two copper wires, each with a 60 Amp fuse in-line waterproof fuseholder for traffic signals, giving #6 traffic signal service wires, and a #6 spare for traffic signal (when specified) on the right leg. The neutral leg is bonded to the ground rod (Bond neutral to ground rod) and continues as the neutral service wire. 3 #6 wires for B.S.L. (Bureau of Street Lighting, see Street Lighting Plan) run from the street lighting side of the fuses.

Section: A service pole stands at the left with a 2" conduit running 10'-0" down its face, then bending at the base and running underground toward the pullbox. The conduit run from pole to pullbox is 5'-0" to 15'-0". The Service Pullbox PB-3 is set flush with the grade, 14" MIN. deep. Inside it a bonding wire joins the conduit bushings, a ground rod is installed below, one Traffic Signal service conduit (2") enters and one street lighting service conduit enters when specified on the Bureau of Street Lighting plan.

Title block: Over Head Service, Dept. of Water & Power, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-79.8. Drawn MT 9-14-11, checked RSM 9-14-11. Approved 10-27-11, Jaime de la Vega, General Manager. Printed page number 86.

One traffic signal service conduit (2").
title: Over Head Service, Dept. of Water & Power

description:
Isometric: The Type II service distribution cabinet with its door open, showing a load center panel inside and the mounting flange base with slotted bolt holes.

A 100 AMPS load center with circuit breakers is mounted on the back panel at the top of the cabinet, 4" below the top of the opening. Two 3" conduits (2-3" CONDUITS) rise into the cabinet from the foundation. The foundation projects 2" above the surface and is 24" deep, with anchor bolts and a ground rod, and break lines show the depth is not fully drawn.

Side view: The cabinet depth is 7-1/4". The 100 AMPS load center is shown on the back panel, with mounting studs at top and bottom and a 1-5/8" offset dimension. A conduit is shown dashed bending out of the foundation at 14" MIN. depth.

Circuit breaker schedule (note 3): 1 each 2 pole 50A, 1 each 1 pole 50A, 1 each 1 pole 30A, 2 each 1 pole 20A.

description:
PVC Conduit System (top diagram): A schematic of service grounding with a Service Pullbox at left, a Controller Pullbox in the middle and a Traffic Signal Cabinet at right. In the service pullbox, three utility conductors AC+, AC- and AC+ come in 'From Utility' through bonded galvanized conduit to the service fuse. The service ground rod is 8FT x 1/2", and a #8 green bond wire connects the conduit bond to the ground rod (marked with an asterisk, with an NC (normally closed) point). Schedule 80 PVC carries a dedicated service of #6 black, #6 green and #6 white (Black, Green, White) plus a #8 green bond wire to the controller pullbox. In the controller pullbox the wires pass through in Schedule 80 PVC, with the #8 green bond wires joined by a compression type fitting between two PVC stubs. The wires continue in Schedule 80 PVC to the traffic signal cabinet, where black, green and white land on the cabinet service block (Ground, AC+, AC-). The #8 green bond wire goes to the cabinet ground rod (8FT x 1/2") and, through a compression type fitting, to the equipment ground bus.

Galvanized Conduit System (bottom diagram): Same layout, but the conduits between pullboxes are bonded galvanized conduit instead of PVC, with a callout 'Use a bushing on all metal conduit' and 'Bonded Galvanized conduit' at the pullbox ends. The #8 green bond wire connects to the conduit bonding at each pullbox. The controller pullbox has a compression type fitting joining the bond wire to the two PVC stubs, and the cabinet ground rod arrangement is the same as in the PVC system.

Title block: Service Grounding Conduit System, sheet 1 of 1. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawing No. S-79.9B. Drawn MT 8-17-11, checked RL 8-17-11, Pr. T.E. SS 9-9-11. Approved September 9, 2011, signed for Jaime de la Vega, General Manager. Printed page number 89.
notes:

PVC Conduit System callouts: Service pullbox. Service fuse. Bonded galvanized conduit. NC. From utility AC+, AC-, AC+. #8 green bond wire. Schedule 80 PVC. Service ground rod: 8FT x 1/2". Dedicated service #6 black, #6 green, #6 white. Black, Green, White. Controller pullbox. Compression type fitting. Traffic signal cabinet. Cabinet service block (Ground, AC+, AC-). Equipment ground bus. Cabinet ground rod: 8FT x 1/2".

Galvanized Conduit System callouts: Use a bushing on all metal conduit. Bonded galvanized conduit. Other callouts as in the PVC system.
title: Service Grounding Conduit System (PVC and Galvanized)
summary: Drawing S-79.9B showing two schematics of service grounding, one for PVC conduit and one for galvanized conduit, running from a service pullbox through a controller pullbox to the traffic signal cabinet. Each carries dedicated #6 black, #6 green and #6 white service wires with a #8 green bond wire, with 8 ft x 1/2 in. ground rods at the service and the cabinet. A ground rod wire clamp (Acorn) is used for each wire, and bushings are required on all metal conduit.

description:
Front view: The front of a Type 332 controller cabinet on its foundation, with the door closed and handle at the right. A raintight box is mounted on the right side of the cabinet near the top, with two small holes: 'Nipple with two 3/4" bushings, See Note 2' and '1/2" hole with rubber bushing'. A 1" grounding bushing (See Note 2) is at the bottom of the box. A 1" galvanized conduit (See Note 2) runs down the cabinet side, through a coupling at the foundation top, then bends and runs underground at 18" MIN. depth 'To Telephone Co. Manhole or Pullbox or to Dept. of Transportation Pullbox'.

Side view: The same box and conduit seen from the side of the cabinet. The box top is 30" below the cabinet top and the conduit is offset 1" from the box edge. The 1" galvanized conduit drops to the coupling at the foundation and down into the ground. Labels match the front view: Type 332 Controller Cabinet, nipple with two 3/4" bushings, 1/2" hole with rubber bushing, 1" grounding bushing, 1" galvanized conduit, coupling, 18" MIN.

title: Service, Telephone ATSAC 332 Cabinet
